items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: And Monk Hazel left with us on tour. And we had Monk Hazel, we had Joe Rodas, I should say the late Joe Rodas on trombone, myself on string bass.

ctx.x: You can meet some real problems. Well, anyhow, there's a lot of bands that we talked about and we'd mentioned the leader. But for example, we never did talk about really who was in Sharky's band and too much of what you did with him.

Well, at the time, I was with the Sharky group. Sharky had called me like five months in advance and he said, Bob, would you like to make a road tour with me? I said, well, sure. But I said, when are you planning on leaving? And he said, oh, I'm about six months from now. I said, well, Sharky, why don't you call me about two months in advance? And then I could more officially give you an answer. You know, I mean, I don't like to plan anything six months in advance. That's pretty far away. So he says, okay. So he…
Did you say who the clarinet player was? Oh, uh... Start at the top. The high note.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: No, I'm talking about having had the pleasure of working with the late Monk Hazel, the late Harry Shields, and the late Almond Hug, and of course the late Sharky's.

ctx.x: Harry, yeah. Larry is his brother who passed away many years ago. Now Larry, the one that was in California, he wrote clarinet, marmalade, plus many other tunes. Oh. No, I'm talking about having had the pleasure of working with the late Monk Hazel, the late Harry Shields, and the late Almond Hug, and of course the late Sharky's. I feel really honored having had the opportunity of working with guys like that. And of course I really enjoyed working with Al Hurd and Pete Fountain, and of course Bob Havens and all…
I haven't heard him in years.
